newsitem.title: USA: Nike fourth-quarter results show slowing growth.
newsitem.headline: Nike fourth-quarter results show slowing growth.

text.p: Nike Inc. said Tuesday its fourth-quarter profits rose 17 percent, reflecting a slowdown in growth that the sports footwear and apparel giant had announced in May to the disappointment of Wall Street.

Nike earned $155.8 million, or 52 cents a share for the quarter that ended May 31, up 17 percent from $133.7 million, or 45 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter. Revenues rose 28 percent to $2.37 billion from $1.85 billion.
The results were at the low end of the prediction Nike issued May 29, which sent the company's stock tumbling and spurred analysts to slash their forecasts.
Nevertheless, Nike sold a record $9.19 billion worth of sneakers, T shirts and other gear in its latest fiscal year, up 42 percent from the $6.47 billion in sales a year earlier.
Capping two years of spectacular growth, Nike said earnings rose 44 percent in the fiscal year to $796 million, or $2.68 a share, compared with $553 million, or $1.88 a share, a year earlier.
Nike said orders for footwear and apparel to be delivered to retailers from June through November totaled $4.9 billion, an increase of 18 percent over year-earlier levels.

While that is far less than "futures" increases averaging more than 40 percent over the past two years, the trend should still be sufficient to ensure another record year, Nike Chairman Philip Knight said in a statement.

"By any standard of measure, fiscal 1997 was the greatest performance in our 25-year history," Knight said. "Over the past two years, we have taken the company formerly known as the industry leader in athletic shoes and transformed it into a global brand franchise with an unprecedented level of market leadership."

Analysts agreed that Nike is poised for continued growth, particularly in markets outside the United States, although they said a slowdown virtually was inevitable after the company has seen its sales nearly double in just two years.
Indeed, Nike executives said in a conference call that the company was on track to meeting its long-term goal of generating sales and earnings growth of 15 percent to 18 percent a year.

Executives said that, based on advance orders, U.S. footwear sales are likely to flatten in the second quarter beginning Sept. 1, but that will be offset by growth in overseas markets, particularly Japan.

For the year just ended, Nike generated 38 percent of its revenues outside the United States, compared with 36 percent a year earlier. Knight has said Nike will get about 50 percent of its sales overseas by the end of the decade.
Nike's U.S. apparel sales virtually doubled last year, while U.S. athletic footwear sales were up a more modest 20 percent.
Nike stock rose 37.5 cents to close at $58 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange ahead of the earnings announcement. The stock peaked at more than $76 in February.
